Replay

MultiplayerPeer connection generations

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Connection generations distinguish successive connections when a backend reuses a numeric peer ID. During one open lifetime, the shared Godot MultiplayerPeer adapter assigns each accepted connection a nonzero, increasing generation. A reused numeric peer ID receives a new generation. Duplicate connect notifications for an active ID preserve its generation. Unknown/disconnected peers report zero. When the counter is exhausted, the adapter refuses new connections instead of wrapping it.

Transport.generation and Received.generation expose this local metadata. ENet uses it directly; the Steam wrapper forwards it. Delay, Router, Fragments and Remap can therefore retire buffered work from a replaced connection using their existing generation checks. It is not transmitted identity or authentication.

A packet kept after Buffer_Too_Small retains its original generation. Disconnect retires that pending copy. Packets may also remain in the backend's FIFO when a connection changes. At each new connect notification, the adapter records how many packets are already queued. Packets from that ID within the earlier queue prefix are discarded; other peers' packets remain deliverable. Only subsequent packets can receive the new generation. Metadata storage remains bounded by the configured live-peer capacity and does not retain a growing set of disconnected IDs.

Backends must expose a FIFO packet queue and notify connection transitions before queueing that connection's packets. The adapter owns polling and reading while attached; external consumers must not remove or reorder its backend packets. Godot's upstream ENet implementation queues received packets separately from its peer registry. The adapter must therefore identify and discard packets queued before the new connection; disconnect does not imply that queue was purged.

Closing the adapter ends all borrowed handles and resets its generation namespace. Close outer wrappers as well before reopening an owner; an old borrowed handle must not be reused against a new owner lifetime. The native creator-rejoin path still explicitly replaces its complete transport when server ID 1 is reused.

This changes local adapter metadata only. Gameplay wire formats, content hashes and checkpoint layouts do not change. Public admission, account identity and provider-specific authentication remain separate requirements.
